record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.original_question: In the same extremal-solution setting, assume the extremal solution u* is unbounded. What can be said about its blow-up set? In particular, if the domain Ω is convex, does the blow-up set reduce to a single point?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6.2 ([16, 34]). Assume u* ∉ L∞(Ω). What can be said about the blow-up set of u*? Does it consist of a single point when Ω is convex?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be a smooth bounded domain, and let $f:[0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be a $C^1$, nondecreasing, convex function with $\lim_{t\to\infty} f(t)/t = +\infty$. For $\lambda \ge 0$, consider the semilinear elliptic problem
$$(P_\lambda)\quad -\Delta u = \lambda f(u)\ \text{in}\ \Omega,\qquad u=0\ \text{on}\ \partial\Omega,\qquad u\ge 0\ \text{in}\ \Omega.$$
It is classical that there exists a finite critical parameter $\lambda^* \in (0,\infty)$ such that:
- for every $\lambda \in [0,\lambda^*)$, problem $(P_\lambda)$ admits a minimal classical solution $u_\lambda \in C^2(\overline{\Omega})$, and the family $\{u_\lambda\}$ is pointwise increasing in $\lambda$;
- for $\lambda > \lambda^*$, no classical solution exists.

The extremal solution is defined as
$$u^*(x) := \lim_{\lambda \uparrow \lambda^*} u_\lambda(x),\qquad x\in\Omega.$$
It is known that $u^* \in H^1_0(\Omega)$ is a weak solution of $(P_{\lambda^*})$.

Assume that $u^* \notin L^\infty(\Omega)$ (the singular case). Define the blow-up set
$$\mathcal{S}(u^*) := \{x_0 \in \overline{\Omega} : \limsup_{x\to x_0} u^*(x) = +\infty\}.$$

(a) Describe the structure of $\mathcal{S}(u^*)$ (for example, its size, location, and dependence on $f$ and $\Omega$).

(b) In particular, prove or disprove: if $\Omega$ is convex, then $\mathcal{S}(u^*)$ consists of a single point.
artifact.category_tag: extremal solutions of semilinear elliptic equations
artifact.status_search_result: The question of describing the blow-up set of the (singular) extremal solution, and in particular whether it must be a single point when the domain is convex, is a long-standing open problem in the theory of extremal solutions. While regularity results (e.g. Cabré–Figalli–Ros-Oton–Serra in dimensions ≤ 9 for convex nondecreasing nonlinearities) and singularity examples in higher dimensions are known, no general description of the blow-up set or proof of single-point blow-up in convex domains appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Stable solutions to semilinear elliptic equations are smooth up to dimension 9
status_evidence.snippet: Boundedness of extremal solutions is established up to dimension 9 for positive, nondecreasing, convex f; singular extremal solutions exist for some f in dimensions ≥ 10.
status_evidence.claim: Regularity is fully understood, but the structure of the blow-up set in the singular case is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Regularity of extremal solutions of semilinear elliptic equations with m-convex nonlinearities
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to study regularity/singularity of extremal solutions; the precise blow-up set in the singular regime remains unspecified.
status_evidence.claim: The question of the blow-up set of a singular extremal solution remains an active open problem.
